prompt: Use the required researcher `prochatgpt_researcher`. Perform a nephrology/endocrine differential-diagnosis and safety investigation for a Spanish lipedema knowledge site—not a generic diuretic overview—on what “pseudo-Bartter syndrome” means in acquired hypokalaemic, hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis and how to explain it without implying that the biochemical pattern proves diuretic abuse or encouraging self-diagnosis. Distinguish recent from remote loop/thiazide exposure; prescribed use from misuse; vomiting or gastric drainage; chloride depletion and volume contraction; mineralocorticoid excess; inherited Bartter and Gitelman syndromes; magnesium deficiency; laxative or diarrhoeal losses; cystic fibrosis or heavy sweat loss; and other important mimics. Explain expected and potentially misleading behavior of urine chloride, urine sodium and potassium, renin/aldosterone, blood pressure, magnesium, kidney function, and diuretic screens, emphasizing how sampling time, ongoing drug action, volume status, and assay limitations can undermine a single result. Audit these claims: pseudo-Bartter is an acquired phenotype rather than a diagnosis of intent; loop/thiazide drugs tend toward alkalosis and potassium/magnesium loss; potassium-sparing agents can cause hyperkalaemia; acetazolamide tends toward metabolic acidosis; and abrupt cessation after chronic exposure may cause edema through persistent RAAS/aldosterone activation, but the public should not receive a rigid time course or universal treatment protocol. Investigate whether “laxatives cause pseudo-Bartter” is too broad and identify edge cases in which diarrhea coexists with alkalosis. Use nephrology reviews, original reports, official drug information, and carefully contextualized eating-disorder literature; do not extrapolate spironolactone protocols to lipedema. Explicitly separate direct lipedema evidence (likely absent), adjacent clinical evidence, mechanistic inference, and anecdote. Report source dates, DOI/PMID, applicable study sizes, full-text/opened status, contradictions, diagnostic traps, safety and urgent red flags, and a short Spanish public translation explaining when to seek medical review without providing a DIY diagnostic or withdrawal algorithm. Filter SEO content, supplement sales, clinics, and unsupported community claims.
